In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the knowledge-generating paradigm change can be modeled in two dimensions: the temporal dimension and the structural one.

the observed knowledge-generating efficiency of innovation systems is a result of self-organization processes that lead to the breaking of old relations, the emergence of new relations, and the emergence of new knowledge-generating paradignms.
the knowledge-generating efficiency is a function of a complex interplay of structural, dynamic and temporal factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the efficiency of the knowledge-generations is a function of the structural effects (the number of dimensions in which the system is organized) and temporal effects (the duration of the cycles in the system).
the efficiency of the innovation systems depends on their structure.
we have found that the dynamics of the knowledge-generations process is a combination of two effects: the structural effect and the temporal effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of innovation is driven by the interaction of the structural and temporal aspects of innovation.
knowledge generation is an emergent phenomenon that cannot be reduced to a linear process.
knowledge generation is not an automatic process, but requires a specific structure and a specific set of relations between actors.
